title: Understanding Your Clinical Nurse Consultant Salary: Hourly to Annual Conversion with Casual Loading and Super
description: Learn how to convert a clinical nurse consultant salary from hourly to annual, including casual loading and super. Use our guide with Fair Work award rates and tax estimates.
salarySummary: For a clinical nurse consultant under the Nurses Award 2020, the minimum hourly rate ranges from $30.00 to $31.56 for RN2 (Clinical Nurse), with higher rates for consultant levels, assuming 38 hours per week.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading for a clinical nurse consultant under the Nurses Award?
faqs.a: Under the Nurses Award 2020, casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate for their classification. For a clinical nurse consultant, this means the casual hourly rate is the base rate plus 25%. For example, if the base rate is $31.56 per hour (RN2 Pay Point 5), the casual rate would be $39.45 per hour. This loading compensates for entitlements like paid leave.

faqs.q: How is super calculated on a clinical nurse consultant salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a clinical nurse consultant earning $60,000 per year, super would be an additional $7,200, paid into your nominated fund. The Australian Taxation Office sets the rules.

faqs.q: How do I use the hourly to annual timesheet for my clinical nurse consultant role?
faqs.a: Visit [the timesheet](/). Enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading). If you are casual, check the box to add 25% loading. The tool multiplies your rate by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks to give an annual gross estimate. It also shows fortnightly pay, tax, Medicare, and super. Remember, this is an estimate and does not include overtime, penalties, or salary sacrifice.

bodyMarkdown:
## Introduction

If you are a clinical nurse consultant or considering this role, understanding how your hourly rate translates into an annual salary is essential for budgeting and comparing offers. The **clinical nurse consultant salary** under the Nurses Award 2020 depends on your classification and experience. This guide explains the conversion, including casual loading and superannuation paid on top, using the latest Fair Work Ombudsman rates.

## The Conversion Formula

The standard formula to estimate annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a full-time load of 38 hours per week, as set by the Nurses Award. For example, a Registered Nurse Level 2 (Clinical Nurse) at Pay Point 1 earns $30.00 per hour. Annual gross would be:

$30.00 × 38 × 52 = $59,280

Higher classifications, such as Clinical Nurse Consultant (often RN3 or above), have higher minimum rates not shown in the provided award extract, but the same formula applies. You can find your exact classification in the award.

### Fortnightly Pay

Fortnightly pay is simply weekly pay multiplied by two. For the example above, weekly pay is $30.00 × 38 = $1,140, so fortnightly is $2,280 before tax.

## Casual Loading

If you work as a casual clinical nurse consultant, you receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. This is detailed in clause 11.1 of the Nurses Award. The loading compensates for not receiving paid leave. To calculate your casual hourly rate:

**Casual rate = minimum hourly rate × 1.25**

For an RN2 at $31.56 per hour (Pay Point 5), the casual rate is $39.45. Annual gross for a casual working 38 hours per week would be:

$39.45 × 38 × 52 = $77,953.20

Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains more. When using [the timesheet](/), enter your base rate without loading, then check the casual box.

## Superannuation Paid on Top

Superannuation is an additional payment made by your employer into a super fund. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is paid on top of your gross pay—it is not deducted from your salary.

For a clinical nurse consultant earning $80,000 per year, super would be $9,600 (12% of $80,000). If your earnings exceed the maximum base, super is capped. The Australian Taxation Office administers these rules.

## Tax and Medicare

Your take-home pay depends on tax and the Medicare levy. For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil up to $18,200
- 15% from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Using the example of $59,280 annual gross, tax would be approximately $8,717 and Medicare $1,186, leaving about $49,377 take-home (excluding super).

## Using the Timesheet

Our [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and see the annual, fortnightly, and weekly estimates with tax and super. It assumes 38 hours per week and no unpaid overtime, penalties, or allowances. For a clinical nurse consultant salary, this gives a solid starting point for negotiations or budgeting.

## Conclusion

Converting your clinical nurse consultant salary from hourly to annual is straightforward with the right formula and award knowledge. Remember that casual loading and super are paid on top, and tax is progressive. For more detailed pay guides, visit our [pay guides](/blog) page. Always check the Fair Work Ombudsman for the latest award rates.
